# APRS symbol and device names, and the symbol icons

`aprs-tables.js` is generated by `tools/vendor_aprs_tables.py` from two
lists that Hessu, OH7LZB, maintains for aprs.fi. Never edit it by hand:
change the inputs and run the tool again.

| Table | Source | Commit | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Symbol names | https://github.com/hessu/aprs-symbol-index, `generated/symbols.dense.json` | `68a273408f` (2014-06-24) | CC BY-SA 4.0 |
| Device names | https://github.com/aprsorg/aprs-deviceid, `tocalls.yaml` | `845e3f89d5` (2026-09-17) | CC BY-SA 2.0 |

The icons, `aprs-symbols-24-{0,1,2}@2x.png`, are copied without change
from https://github.com/hessu/aprs-symbols, `png/` at commit `f2286a9cd4`
(2024-10-10): the primary table, the alternate table and the overlay
characters, 48 px per symbol, drawn at 24 px. The set is released "to the
APRS community ... for free" and asks for a pointer to its source. A few
symbols are vector copies of company logos (Apple, Microsoft, Kenwood),
whose owners hold those marks; see that repository's COPYRIGHT.md.

All three ask that the source is credited. The credit is here, in
the header of `aprs-tables.js`, and in the small print of the RF tab.

## How it is used

The RF tab reads `window.SonoranAprsTables` to name what an APRS packet
carries in code:

- `symbols`: the symbol a station chose, such as `/#`, becomes
  "Digipeater". An overlay replaces the table character (`S#` is the
  `\#` symbol with an `S` on it), so the page looks up `\` and the code.
- `tocalls`: the destination of a plain packet, such as `APMI06`, names
  the software or radio that sent it. `?` matches any character, `n` a
  digit and `*` any run. The list is sorted most specific first, and
  the page takes the first match.

- The icons: each sheet is 16 symbols wide and 6 high, starting at `!`
  (character 33). A symbol's cell is `code - 33`. An overlay symbol is
  the alternate table's cell with the overlay sheet's cell for the
  letter or digit drawn on top.

Nothing here decodes a packet. The agent does that; this only names
what it decoded.
